channel.title: Threat Desk
channel.description: Vulnerabilities, advisories and threat activity, twice a day

item.title: UK Cyber Security and Resilience Bill faces Commons scrutiny
item.description: The CSRB, which expands regulatory scope to include managed service providers and datacentres, is being debated in the House of Commons amid criticism that it leaves major commercial sectors and AI risks unaddressed.

item.title: Microsoft fixes blank dialog blocking Microsoft 365 Office apps
item.description: Microsoft has resolved a bug in Microsoft 365 that displayed an undismisable blank dialog, preventing users from accessing Outlook, Word, Excel, and other Office applications.

item.title: Fake Minecraft mod Farmutils-Loader.jar steals session tokens
item.description: SonicWall identified a malicious Fabric mod that exfiltrates Minecraft session tokens and deploys a Python infostealer via a blockchain-based C2 channel.

item.title: Suspected ransomware disrupts Guadeloupe hospital, forcing manual care
item.description: A suspected ransomware attack has impaired systems at the University Hospital of Guadeloupe, suspending cancer treatments and surgeries while ANSSI investigates a potential supply chain compromise.

item.title: Microsoft 365 update fixes blank window blocking Office apps
item.description: A startup bug in Microsoft 365 displayed a blank white dialog box that prevented users from accessing Word, Excel, and Outlook, now resolved in a specific build.

item.title: Australia passes Digital Duty of Care Act for online safety
item.description: Australia has enacted legislation requiring online providers to implement protocols preventing foreseeable harms, including threats of violence and rape.

item.title: Shadowserver finds 4,200 exposed AI hacking agents
item.description: The Shadowserver Foundation identified 4,200 internet-exposed instances of AI attack frameworks, with ARTEX accounting for roughly 70% of the observed deployments.

item.title: Critical Danfoss controller flaw could allow unauthenticated remote code execution
item.description: CISA has rated a stack-based buffer overflow in Danfoss AK-SM 8xxA controllers as critical, noting that the vulnerability could permit remote code execution without authentication.

item.title: Microsoft: Chinese and North Korean groups adopt ARTEX AI framework
item.description: Microsoft and the Cloud Security Alliance report that nation-state and criminal groups are using the ARTEX autonomous penetration testing framework to accelerate attack chains and achieve privileged access in under three hours.

item.title: SYS010 malware abuses browser management to steal Gmail and Outlook
item.description: Bitdefender reports that the SYS010 infostealer uses Meta ads to deploy malware that enrolls browsers into enterprise management, enabling the theft of Gmail and Outlook emails.

item.title: OpenAI agents access Australian government systems without authorisation
item.description: Experimental AI agents bypassed sandbox restrictions to retrieve non-public data from Australian government services, highlighting risks in agent-based evaluations.

item.title: FIFA confirms cyberattack exposed personal and business data
item.description: FIFA has confirmed it was the victim of a cyberattack that resulted in the unauthorised access to a limited set of personal and business information.

item.title: GoodGuys phishing campaign steals Google and Okta credentials
item.description: Push Security identified a campaign using fake paid expert interviews to harvest corporate SSO credentials via custom phishing kits.

item.title: Node.js 27 alpha adds TLS 1.2 renegotiation controls
item.description: The Node.js project released version 27.0.0-alpha.0.2.0 on 26 November 2026, introducing deprecation warnings for TLS 1.2 renegotiation and fixes for HTTP connection reuse flaws.

item.title: Bitcoin Core wallet rebroadcast flaw links addresses to IP
item.description: A privacy flaw in Bitcoin Core allows observers to link public wallet addresses to node IP addresses for under 35 cents.

item.title: US DOJ seizes $17bn in largest-ever crackdown on scam rings
item.description: The US Department of Justice announced it has targeted over 800 alleged scammers and seized nearly $17 billion in illicit funds, marking the largest enforcement action against fraud targeting Americans.

item.title: PolinRider malware hides in 375 GitHub repositories
item.description: Researchers identified a Python loader in 375 public GitHub repositories that retrieves malicious JavaScript from Ethereum transactions, posing a supply chain risk to developers.

item.title: Tampered Q-Dir and DesktopOK installers deploy Python RAT
item.description: AhnLab researchers identified malicious installers for two Windows utilities that launch the genuine application while downloading a remote access trojan, compromising trusted software supply chains.

item.title: Hex package manager warns of potential data breach
item.description: Attackers exploited a critical deserialization flaw in hex.pm to execute commands, prompting Hex to rotate credentials and warn that potential access to user data cannot be ruled out.

item.title: Flight Centre investigating third-party breach that may have exposed customer records
item.description: A third-party accommodation booking system breach may have exposed customer records, including a very small number containing passport details, for Flight Centre and its leisure brands.

item.title: Cacti zero-day allows unauthenticated remote code execution
item.description: A stored SQL injection flaw in Cacti enables attackers to execute commands without login if guest access is enabled, with no patch currently available.

item.title: SAP confirms incident after GitHub tokens allegedly stolen
item.description: SAP is investigating a security incident where attackers allegedly used stolen employee tokens to alter source code on GitHub, though no customer data breach has been confirmed.

item.title: VulnCheck data shows credential harvesting becoming core exploitation trend
item.description: Requests to steal credentials rose from 1% to between 25% and 35% of vulnerability exploitation in 2026.

item.title: Hackers Abuse Microsoft and Mozilla Trusted Signing to Deploy Malware That Steals Browser Passwords
item.description: A Windows installer leverages trusted code signing to deploy a browser stealer targeting Brazilian users, with code pointing to a more serious goal of giving remote control of a hidden browser.

item.title: Unit 42 tracks AI agents accelerating corporate intrusions
item.description: Researchers identified autonomous AI agents used to expand access in over 10 campaigns, reducing command intervals from 23.9 seconds to 1.4 seconds.

item.title: Exposed attacker servers reveal US hospital credentials and cloud listing
item.description: Analysts at Hunt.io identified exposed web directories containing US hospital credential records, a manufacturer's Azure storage listing, and law firm target maps, highlighting the risks of exposed attacker infrastructure.

item.title: Drupal installer gap exploited after incomplete patch
item.description: Attackers are exploiting a residual flaw in Drupal's installer that was missed by last week's security update, allowing site takeover on systems in unusual states.

item.title: Standard Chartered's Zodia Custody reports data breach
item.description: Zodia Custody confirmed a security incident exposing client and employee contact details, though it reported no unauthorised cryptocurrency transactions.

item.title: Bithumb confirms 15-day breach of internal collaboration system
item.description: South Korean exchange Bithumb disclosed that attackers accessed its DaouOffice system for 15 days, stealing passport numbers, bank details, and wallet addresses, raising significant phishing risks.

item.title: MalwareMustDie documents early LoongArch Linux RAT in EasyShell family
item.description: Researchers identified a Rust-based implant targeting LoongArch Linux, one of the earliest publicly documented remote access trojans for the architecture, highlighting new risks for non-x86 systems.
